scope: Relative references for shape-dependent contact, scoped to each stated goal and entry. Different objectives confound comparisons; these are design judgments, not calibrated human-difficulty scores.

levels.label: Contact and continuation
levels.criteria: Prepare one tool-target relationship, establish operable contact, and continue passage work.

levels.label: Released-tool reuse
levels.criteria: Release a constrained tool and reuse its different members against successive targets, with recovery and changing input access.

levels.label: Shared-space coordination
levels.criteria: Coordinate competing full footprints, withdraw and reuse tools, switch roles, and establish more than one passage in one continued route.

difficulty.rationale: Provisional structural inventory of the existing case: one prepared rear-contact pair releases a boundary restriction and enables further passage work. It is the comparison foundation, not an easy-room claim.

Provisional structural inventory of the existing case: a released target becomes a tool, crosses separated input/work areas and operates two later targets. This adds role transition and repeated recovery to the single-pair foundation; the gem goal differs.

The supplied relative higher placement is mapped to Shared-space coordination: competing footprints repeatedly change later input access, several pairs switch roles, and one continuous route opens two passages. This is a user judgment with structural rationale, not a playtest or solver-count ranking.
